newsitem.title: OMAN: Gulf Air board meets on airline's performance.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Air board meets on airline's performance.

text.p: The board of directors of Gulf Air met on Wednesday to look into ways to improve the debt-ridden airline's performance, Oman's official news agency ONA said.

"During the positive meeting, the airline's administration was asked to work on improving its path on proper commercial and administrative basis," Majed bin Said al-Rawahi, the airline's chief executive officer, told ONA.
"The issue of raising the company's paid up capital to 250 million Bahraini dinars ($657 million) from 150 million dinars now was also discussed," he added.
Rawahi said the board would ask the general assembly to hold an emergency meeting to discuss the possibility of such an increase and of taking measures to shape up the Bahrain-based regional airline.
"Satisfaction with the airline's current situation could lead the company to huge difficulties that might lead to its bankruptcy," Rawahi warned.
He gave no further details and did not say when the general assembly would meet.
The airline is jointly owned by the governments of Bahrain, Qatar, Oman and Abu Dhabi.
The London-based Arabic newspaper Asharq al-Awsat said on Sunday the carrier needs urgent cash to finance its estimated $1 billion in debts.
It said while Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates had backed the idea of pumping in more cash to help pay its debts, Oman and Qatar appeared to be against such a move.
"UAE and Bahrain will demand that they buy the Qatari and Omani stakes in return for pumping liquidity into Gulf Air," it said, quoting unnamed Gulf sources.
Bahrain's Finance and National Economy Minister Ibrahim Abdel-Karim, accompanied by civil aviation officials, flew to Abu Dhabi on Saturday to review ways of servicing the airline's debts.
The airline plans to lease more aircraft and cut unprofitable routes to help it return to profit after a $159 million loss in 1995. ($1=0.38 Bahraini dinars)
